title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. In the 1986 'Ateliers' notes Grothendieck builds a combinatorial, purely order-theoretic model of a one-dimensional 'tame' space. Start from an ordered set I, presumably totally ordered, since the intervals I_{<a}, I_{a,b}, I_{>b} require it. Attach two sets Ω0 and Ω1, each with at most one element: these are the origin and the end, when they exist (previous page).

The set M = M(I,Ω0,Ω1) consists of the 'structures' (strata) of the line:
- points a ∈ I;
- open intervals I_{<a}, I_{a,b}, I_{>b}.
M carries the induced 'lexicographic' order. The empty ordered set is allowed: it represents the indivisible open interval, and then M(∅) = {∅}.

On this page.
1. For regions, polygons, constructible parts, 'rapports' and connectedness, no further hypothesis on I is needed. The added hypotheses, such as density ('divisible'), appear on the next page.
2. When polygons are seen as sub-objects relative to a diagram (a finite set of cut points, a 'trame'), it is convenient for the main statements to take a diagram containing the boundary ∂I := Ω0 ∪ Ω1.
3. The main structural statement concerns the 'region structure' induced on a constructible part, in particular on a constructible polygon 𝔓:
   a) M(𝔓) is a 'direct sum' (to be defined) of the M(𝔓_i) over the connected components 𝔓_i of 𝔓, some of which may be single points {a}.
   b) If 𝔓 is connected, M(𝔓) is again of the form M(I',Ω0',Ω1').
4. Formula (*) describes the new ordered set, under the reading a = inf δ𝔓, b = sup δ𝔓 (δ𝔓 = the boundary/diagram points of 𝔓). I' is the set of points s of I such that:
   - a ≤ s ≤ b;
   - s together with δ𝔓 is still an admissible diagram (illegible condition b);
   - if s is an endpoint a or b, then s belongs to the point-part 𝔓_0 of 𝔓.
   Ω0' and Ω1' are, accordingly, a or b when these endpoints lie in 𝔓 (next page).

In modern terms: a connected constructible subset of a 'line' is an interval. That interval is again a line of the same type, with endpoints present or absent according to whether they belong to the set. A general constructible set is the ordered (ordinal/lexicographic) sum of such pieces. This is the order-theoretic shadow of one-dimensional cell decomposition in o-minimality. It is also akin to the closure of 'interval types' under restriction.

Margin notes:
- the case 𝔓 = {a} is trivial;
- a warning that the description needs a restriction on the components of 𝔓 (illegible).

The next page completes this: I' is the ordered sum of the supports |X|° of the structures X in 𝔓, Ω0 and Ω1 are given by origin and end, and density ('divisible') is introduced.
errors: 'I un ordonné' should be a totally ordered set; the interval strata and the inf/sup constructions presuppose a total order.

a = inf δ𝔓 and b = sup δ𝔓 need not exist as points of I if 𝔓 contains an unbounded piece such as I_{<c}. These cases have to go through Ω0/Ω1 being empty, which (*) does not state explicitly. The next page repairs this with the origin/end formalism.

The 'somme directe' of the M(𝔓_i) is explicitly left undefined ('à définir!'). The bottom 'Attention' note signals that the description (*) is valid only under a restriction on 𝔓, so the statement on this page is incomplete as written.

ideas.what: Line model M(I,Ω0,Ω1): an ordered set with optional endpoints, whose strata are points and open intervals; the empty ordered set stands for the indivisible open interval.
ideas.modern_name: Combinatorial 1-dimensional stratified space; interval objects; dense linear orders with endpoints (o-minimal base case)
ideas.usually_credited_to: o-minimality: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn (1984-86); interval categories: Joyal
ideas.where_published: Tame topology programme announced in Esquisse d'un programme §5-6 (1984); this formalism is unpublished

ideas.what: A constructible part is the ordered sum of its connected components; a connected constructible polygon induces again a line M(I',Ω0',Ω1').
ideas.modern_name: 1-dimensional cell decomposition / definable connected sets are intervals
ideas.usually_credited_to: o-minimal structure theory (Pillay–Steinhorn, van den Dries)

ideas.what: Choosing a diagram (trame) containing the boundary ∂I = Ω0 ∪ Ω1 for the statement of the main results.
ideas.modern_name: Refining a stratification to include boundary strata

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a purely order-theoretic, hypothesis-free 1-dimensional model for 'régions/polygones/rapports' as a building block for tame topology. The 'direct sum' of such line-structures is left undefined. The programme is visible but elementary here; it is only potentially of interest as a documented step of his unpublished tame-topology work.
missed.quote: M(𝔓) est la somme directe (à définir!) des M(𝔓_i)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it documents how Grothendieck intended to axiomatize tame topology combinatorially, in parallel with o-minimality, which he does not cite.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is an elementary structural lemma: a connected constructible subset of an ordered 'line' is again a line of the same type. It is well known in o-minimal terms. It is of historical interest only, as part of his unpublished 1986 tame-topology formalism.
transcription_corrections: 'elles-mêmes à des polygones constructibles' is better read 'elles-mêmes ou des polygones constructibles 𝔓' (the 'ou' is uncertain).
In the result, 'et une de la forme {a}, a∈I' is a superscript insertion meaning that some components may be single points {a}.
Margin: 'le cas 𝔓={a} est trivial, et naturellement le cas ... (avec [?])' is followed by the definitions 'a = inf δ𝔓, b = sup δ𝔓', which define a, b in (*).
Line 3: the insertion over 'qui' reads 'et connexités', replacing a crossed-out 'qui'.
